items.title: Bill Mays interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 5, 2025
items.q: If I heard something that Oscar Peterson or Bill Evans or McCoy Tyner did I’d sit at the piano and play it and I would notate it and I would transpose it around the keyboard so I was learning, yes, licks and patterns and full solos

ctx.x: Yes, “slide with the situation.” I like that.

Be a good team member, which I think is incredibly important if you want to be a professional musician. So, but when I heard those people and those records I just fell in love with jazz and that began also a period of just again figuring things out on my own. If I heard something that Oscar Peterson or Bill Evans or McCoy Tyner did I’d sit at the piano and play it and I would notate it and I would transpose it around the keyboard so I was learning, yes, licks and patterns and full solos at the time and in so…
Did you have to sell your parents on this career path?
